marriage.q1: How will you manage your money once married?
marriage.q1a: We'll have a joint account to manage everything together.
marriage.q1b: We'll keep separate accounts + a joint account for shared expenses.
marriage.q1c: We haven't discussed this clearly yet.
marriage.q1d: We haven't agreed and it's already causing tension.
marriage.q2: In case of a significant income difference, how do you handle shared expenses?
marriage.q2a: Each contributes proportionally to their income.
marriage.q2c: The wealthier one pays for everything, without really discussing it.
marriage.q3: Do you have an aligned vision on savings and investments?
marriage.q3a: Yes, we share the same priorities and have set common goals.
marriage.q3b: We don't have the same habits yet but we're ready to discuss it.
marriage.q3c: One saves, the other spends, and it creates friction.
marriage.q4: Have you discussed debt management (loans, credit) before marriage?
marriage.q4a: Yes, we're transparent about our respective financial situations.
marriage.q4b: Partially, there are still gray areas.
marriage.q5a: Yes, both of us, and we agree on the timing.
marriage.q5b: No, both of us, it's a conscious decision.
marriage.q5c: Yes both of us, but we disagree on timing or number.
marriage.q5d: One wants them, the other doesn't know or doesn't want them.
marriage.q6: If you have children, who will mainly handle their daily upbringing?
marriage.q6a: We share equally, we've discussed it.
marriage.q6b: We'll adapt based on circumstances (work, availability).
marriage.q6c: We assume one will take the lead but haven't really talked about it.
marriage.q7: Do you share the same vision of how to raise your children?
marriage.q7a: Yes, we share the same core educational values.
marriage.q7b: We have some differences but can talk about them.
marriage.q7c: We have very different views and it's not yet resolved.
marriage.q8: How do you manage the relationship with your respective in-laws?
marriage.q8a: We get along well and have established healthy boundaries together.
marriage.q8b: It's sometimes complicated but we stick together.
marriage.q8c: One of us endures the in-laws without it being discussed.
marriage.q9: How are household chores divided between you?
marriage.q9a: 50/50, we've found a balance that works for us.
marriage.q9b: Not exactly 50/50 but each contributes in their own way, without frustration.
marriage.q9c: One does almost everything, and it doesn't bother the other.
marriage.q9d: One does more than the other, and it creates tension.
marriage.q10: Do you have the same standards of cleanliness and organization at home?
marriage.q10a: Yes, or at least compatible, no conflict there.
marriage.q10b: We have differences but know how to adapt.
marriage.q11: If the mental load is unbalanced (organizing, planning, groceries…), what happens?
marriage.q11a: We've identified it together and are working to better balance it.
marriage.q11b: One carries more but it's acknowledged and being improved.
marriage.q11c: One carries everything and the other doesn't really realize it.
marriage.q12: Do you have compatible religious or spiritual beliefs?
marriage.q12a: Yes, we share the same beliefs or fully respect each other on this.
marriage.q12b: We have differences but it's never been a major issue.
marriage.q12c: It's a source of tension and we haven't found balance.
marriage.q13: Are your core values (honesty, fidelity, family, freedom…) aligned?
marriage.q13a: Yes, we share the same essential values.
marriage.q13c: No, we have quite opposing views on certain key values.
marriage.q14: Do you share the same political views or at least mutual respect for differences?
marriage.q14a: We're aligned or fully respect our differences.
marriage.q14b: We have disagreements but they don't create deep conflicts.
marriage.q14c: Our political differences create real tensions.
marriage.q15: Are you comfortable with each other's friend circles?
marriage.q15a: Yes, we get along well with each other's friends and feel comfortable.
marriage.q15b: We don't see them much but without tensions.
marriage.q15c: One doesn't appreciate the other's friends, and it's a source of conflict.

marriage.q16a: Yes, completely, we trust each other.
marriage.q16b: Generally yes, with some moments of discomfort.
marriage.q16c: No, it's often a source of tension or control.
marriage.q17: Do you have a healthy balance between couple time and individual time?
marriage.q17a: Yes, we've found a good balance.
marriage.q17b: We're in the process of finding it.
marriage.q17c: One always wants more time together or apart, and it's problematic.
marriage.q18: Are you both satisfied with your intimate life?
marriage.q18a: Yes, we communicate about it and are well aligned.
marriage.q18b: There are things to improve but we can talk about it.
marriage.q18c: It's a taboo topic or a source of dissatisfaction on both sides.
marriage.q19: Do you have the same definition of fidelity?
marriage.q19a: Yes, absolutely, we're on the same page.
marriage.q19b: We've had this conversation and clarified things.
marriage.q19c: We've never really talked about it clearly.
marriage.q20: In case of distance or asymmetric desire, how do you react?
marriage.q20a: We talk about it openly and look for solutions together.
marriage.q20b: It's difficult but we try to address it.
marriage.q20c: We ignore it or it creates silent tensions.
marriage.q21: Do you share the same vision of where you want to live (city, countryside, country)?
marriage.q21b: We have different preferences but are ready to compromise.
marriage.q21c: We have very different views and it's not resolved.
marriage.q22: Are your respective career ambitions compatible with your shared life plan?
marriage.q22a: Yes, we mutually support each other's ambitions.
marriage.q22b: There are trade-offs to make but we're open to discussing them.
marriage.q22c: Our ambitions conflict, and we don't know how to handle it yet.
marriage.q23: In case of geographical mobility (transfer, opportunity elsewhere), how do you approach it?
marriage.q23a: We would decide together considering both projects.
marriage.q23b: We haven't really thought about it but would assess at that time.
marriage.q23c: One would inevitably follow the other without really having a say.

marriage.q24a: Yes, we have clearly defined shared projects.
marriage.q24b: We have desires but nothing concrete yet.
marriage.q24c: We don't really envision things together.
marriage.q25: When you have a major disagreement, how does it go?
marriage.q25a: We listen to each other, seek compromise, it usually ends well.
marriage.q25b: It's sometimes difficult but we manage.
marriage.q25c: It often escalates or one gives in without conviction.

marriage.q26a: Yes, we've learned to communicate without attacking.
marriage.q26c: Difficult conversations often end in hurt.

marriage.q27a: Yes, we reconcile sincerely and move forward.
marriage.q27b: It takes time but we get there.
marriage.q27c: Resentment often lingers, we bring up old conflicts.
marriage.q28: Have you discussed your respective emotional needs and how to feel supported?
marriage.q28a: Yes, we know each other well on this and respond to it.
marriage.q28b: Partially, there are still things to explore.
marriage.q28c: No, we've never really asked ourselves this question.
marriage.q29: Would you be willing to see a couples therapist if you went through a serious crisis?
marriage.q29a: Yes, both of us, without hesitation.
marriage.q29b: One is open, the other more reluctant.
marriage.q29c: No, neither of us is in favor.
marriage.q30: In summary, do you feel you're truly ready to get married?
marriage.q30a: Yes, both of us, clearly and serenely.
marriage.q30b: We think so, but with some doubts.
marriage.q30c: One is ready, the other much less so.
marriage.q30d: We're not sure, that's why we're taking this test.
marriage.r1_d: Let's be honest: your test reveals that several important topics are not yet resolved between you. This is not a verdict on your love, it's a signal about your readiness. Getting married without aligning on these points is like building a house on incomplete foundations. What this test is telling you is to take more time. Talk, debate, explore your disagreements. Ideally with the help of a couples therapist or marriage counselor. Marriage is not a deadline, it's a milestone that deserves to be reached at the right time.
marriage.r2_d: You clearly have solid foundations. On many essential points, you're aligned, and that matters enormously. But this test also highlighted blind spots, topics you may have avoided or not explored deeply enough. The good news: you still have time to talk, adjust, and find compromises. Note the questions where you scored 0 or 1, that's where your real work lies before the big day.
marriage.r3_d: Congratulations. This test confirms it: you seem truly ready. You've built serious foundations together, on finances, values, daily life, intimacy, and projects. No test can guarantee a happy marriage, because happiness is built day by day. But you seem to have the tools, communication, and willingness to do it. Go for it with confidence, and keep talking to each other as you did during this test.
